comment: HPFT lab registry. Units: rate_bps absolute; PCC converts to 2^20-of-linerate units (line = 200 Gb/s).

rdma_flowtags.comment: per-(src,dst) PCC flowtags, probed via 0xdea 2026-07-11; sgpu03/sgpu04 added 2026-08-23. The tag hashes (src function, dst function) and is stable across QP recreation, IP choice and reflash. KNOWN COLLISION: src vf1 and src vf2 produce identical tags for every dst (rows below are equal), so vf1->X and vf2->X RDMA budgets are inseparable at the RP - never schedule both concurrently. tx_agent_e keys RDMA budgets by 'src>dst' with fallback to the per-vnic flowtag.  CARD-INDEPENDENT (2026-08-23): sgpu03 and sgpu04 return the same tag as sgpu01 for all four straight pairs, so the hash reads the function INDEX, not the card. Each sender DPU runs its own RP, so identical tags on different senders are not a collision. The vf1/vf2 SOURCE collision noted above is a property of the index hash and therefore applies to every sender node alike. The sgpu03/sgpu04 cross-pair rows are carried over from that argument, not probed one by one.

policy.comment: design.md §3.2. VM == vnic in this lab. weight = W_i (inter-tenant); max_rate_bps = MaxRate_i (null = uncapped); class_weights = W_{i,TCP}/W_{i,RDMA}. per_sender_weights: 'dst_vnic|class|src_vnic' -> u (absent = 1). Receiver scheduler reads dst-VM params; sender tree reads src-VM params. MaxRate = 60G re-derived 2026-08-23 for the four-node lab: every p1 now runs at 200 Gb/s (the receiver was the last 100G port and was raised with the rest), so C' = 194G over 4 dst VMs is 48.5G each. The rule is unchanged from the 100G derivation - 4*MaxRate must exceed C' so the ROOT layer binds under full load, while one VM alone stays capped below the link so the VM-cap layer is still reachable. 4*60 = 240G > 194G satisfies the first, 60G < 200G the second. Leaving MaxRate at 30G would have made 4*30 = 120G < 194G and put the lab back in the state the 100G note warns about: the receiver-downlink (incast) bottleneck structurally unreachable, every run exercising only the VM-cap layer.

control.comment: Scheme-E control plane addressing. telemetry: host -> its DPU's in-band ctl IP (PF1 SF on underlay-p1, rides the p1/switch data path per design_e §3.4 user note). pace_shim: sender host -> shim addr as reachable from that host's DPU (tmfifo). tree_stub_bps = static Tree_f until M5's sender tree. rate_export: receiver host -> its DPU rx_agent (tmfifo), fresh kernel-path byte counter for class attribution (2026-07-11).

e_params.comment: design.md §6 (tracking-audit law). RESPONSE LAW: the receiver synthesises one target per flow-set, u_f = ceil_f*(1-gamma*s_f) (§3.4), and the sender does first-order tracking in log space, R <- R*(u/R)^(k*T) (§4.2). Fairness still lives entirely in the receiver's water-filling, not in the law. Params are wall-clock quantities (rate constants in s^-1, integrals in bits), so they do not need retuning when period_ms changes -- there is no ref_period_ms scaling any more. k=20 s^-1 is capped by target staleness (k*tau_eff <~ 0.4, tau_eff ~20ms); gamma=0.25 sets both the audit discount band (u >= 0.75*ceil) and the audit-loop damping (zeta = 0.5*sqrt(k*V/(gamma*ceil))); V = v_seconds*headroom*C = 1.6 Gbit is a wall-clock excess-integral: it must NOT scale with the control period, and it IS anchored on C, the downlink bottleneck capacity the receiver actually schedules against (100G here), not on the NIC port line rate -- ehat scales with C, so V must too or the audit loop's damping becomes link-rate dependent (design.md §3.3). rx_agent reads C from the uplink and recomputes V whenever the link speed changes. HEADROOM=0.08 (2026-07-29, overlay-resident): 3% queue-warning + ~5% VxLAN encap tax (inner-byte ledger vs outer-byte wire, measured 4.99% at 1500 MTU); covers inner packets >= ~625 B, smaller-packet overshoot falls back to tenant CC. V IS NOT DERIVED FROM HEADROOM: the real rule is V = 4*zeta^2*gamma*ehat*/k at the typical contention point (design_theory par.3; ehat*=23G, zeta=1/sqrt(2) => V=576 Mbit, revalidated by results/vtune_20260729). v_seconds=0.072 is only the dial that lands V there through the legacy v_sec*headroom*C packaging -- when headroom or C' changes, re-solve V from the zeta rule and re-set v_seconds, do NOT let V drift; design_theory §3 shows it lands 1% from the optimal-damping inverse V = 4*zeta^2*gamma*ehat_star/k at zeta=1/sqrt(2), which is post-hoc confirmation, not a derivation -- re-derive it if the tenant count, flow count, link rate or loop delay changes. Derivations and tuning rules: hpft-design/docs/design_theory.md.

nodes_comment: Every node carries BOTH planes (rx_agent + tx_agent + PCC executor); which one runs is a per-experiment role, not a per-node property. tools/lab-infra/deploy_check.sh reads this list, so adding a node here is the only edit needed to bring it into the sync loop.
